selections.summary: Defines a behavior-based compression rate for LoRA adapters and finds that weight reconstruction error can misrepresent retained fine-tuning gains.
selections.relevance: Directly addresses low-rank compressibility, singular directions, and corrupted training data.

evidence.quote: near one bit per value, the adaptive code achieves lower relative weight RMSE than uniform quantization (0.54 versus 0.56), yet retains only 3% of the held-out gain, compared with 86% for the uniform code.

selections.summary: Finds contrasting LoRA spectral and subspace dynamics in supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, with controlled comparisons implicating group-mean baseline subtraction.
selections.relevance: Connects LoRA optimization to effective rank and singular-subspace motion.

evidence.quote: Controlled comparisons identify group-mean baseline subtraction as a key source of these differences.

selections.summary: ResQAdam preserves a QAT momentum residual while compressing optimizer state. Its reported peak-memory savings come with a small throughput decrease versus AdamW.
selections.relevance: Directly informs memory, quality, and speed tradeoffs for low-rank optimizer-state compression.

evidence.quote: This efficiency directly translates to a 15.3% to 19.5% reduction in total peak memory.
The training throughput decreases by less than 2% compared to standard AdamW in all evaluated cases.

selections.summary: Adds an SVD-free Rényi-2 effective-rank penalty to LoRA training and reports lower mean Wiki perplexity at tested ranks of at least 16.
selections.relevance: Tests whether spectral regularization can change adapter rank utilization without substantially worsening the training objective.

selections.summary: GEAR uses the normal spectrum to guide LoRA rank expansion and reports an improved LLaMA3-8B commonsense score with fewer trainable parameters.
selections.relevance: Addresses the geometry and practical behavior of dynamically ranked LoRA updates.

evidence.quote: On LLaMA3-8B, it raises the average commonsense score from 86.61 to 88.45 while reducing trainable parameters from 42.0M to 14.4M.

selections.summary: Shows that low stable rank need not mean that an LLM weight update is well represented by a small number of singular components.
selections.relevance: Clarifies which spectral rank measures are useful when judging low-rank compressibility.

selections.relevance: Informs optimization-schedule evaluation and scale-dependent quality tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: Matched intervention and reference runs share initialization, data order, and learning-rate schedule.

selections.summary: Uses active learning to approximate LLM document reranking at a controlled evaluation budget; its strongest reported result is for verbose queries.
